title: "AI Crawler Observatory · Compare"

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML
import charts
import pagedata

facts = pd.read_parquet("data/policy_facts.parquet")
sig = pd.read_parquet("data/sector_signals.parquet")
c = pagedata.compare(facts, sig)
dates = sorted(c["snapshot"].unique())
snapshot_label = dates[0] if len(dates) == 1 else f"{dates[0]} to {dates[-1]}"
top = c.sort_values("Block GPTBot by name", ascending=False).iloc[0]
low = c.sort_values("Block GPTBot by name").iloc[0]
news_top = int((c["top sector"] == "news").sum())
central = f"{c['central sites'].min()} to {c['central sites'].max()}"
```

HTML(pagedata.country_nav("compare"))

## How to read it {#read}

Every figure is a share of the sites we could observe in that country's latest
snapshot. The samples are built with the same rules, and every country's sectors
take Italy's proportions, so the overall shares compare like with like.

Two strata are worth reading on their own. **News** is the sector that blocks
GPTBot by name most often in `{python} news_top` of `{python} len(c)` countries.
**Central government** is the one public-sector tier large enough in every
sample (`{python} central` observable sites) to compare; regional and local
tiers are not.

All fetches run from Italy. Sites that refuse foreign visitors — betting
operators in the United Kingdom and Spain especially — are unobservable from
here and left out, so those countries' figures cover the sites we could read.
Each country page has the detail; the sampling rules are in
[sample/METHOD.md](https://github.com/mxdangelo/aicrawl-census/blob/main/sample/METHOD.md).
